name: Peru
summary: A republic on the Pacific coast of South America, independent from Spain since 1821, home to the former heartland of the Inca Empire.

knownFor.label: Ceviche
knownFor.note: Raw fish cured in lime juice, a national dish.

knownFor.label: Machu Picchu
knownFor.note: Inca site made world-famous after 1911; now Peru’s most visited place.

knownFor.label: Guano boom
knownFor.note: Bird droppings sold as fertiliser made Peru rich in the mid-1800s.

location.value: Western South America, on the Pacific; about 1.3 million km².

terrain.value: A dry coastal desert, the high Andes and the Amazon rainforest.

climate.value: Desert on the coast, cold in the highlands, tropical in the Amazon.

resources.value: Copper, silver, gold, fish (anchovies), guano historically.

urbanisation.value: Lima holds about a third of the people.

disease.value: Cholera epidemic (1991); high COVID-19 death rate.

migration.value: Migration from the highlands to Lima; Chinese and Japanese immigrants.

economicBase.value: Mining, fishing, farming exports and tourism.

tradeRoutes.value: Exports to China, the US and Europe.

moneyAndTax.value: The sol; hyperinflation in the late 1980s.

inequality.value: Large gaps between Lima and rural Andean regions.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic; military governments at times (1968–80).

keyRulers.value: Simón Bolívar and José de San Martín (independence). Ramón Castilla. Juan Velasco Alvarado. Alberto Fujimori.

succession.value: Elections, often interrupted by coups and impeachments.

stability.value: The Shining Path conflict (1980–2000) killed about 70,000 people.

eliteConflict.value: Frequent clashes between presidents and Congress.

armyAndTech.value: Armed forces with a history of political involvement.

majorWars.value: War of the Pacific with Chile (1879–83); conflicts with Ecuador.

territoryChange.value: Lost southern provinces to Chile after 1883.

alliancesRivals.value: Member of the Andean Community and the Pacific Alliance.

inventions.value: Few major inventions; strong archaeology and potato research (International Potato Center).

scienceEducation.value: San Marcos University (1551) is the oldest in the Americas.

communicationTransport.value: Railways over the Andes (Central Railway, among the highest in the world).

languageWriting.value: Spanish, Quechua and Aymara are official.

artsArchitecture.value: Writers such as Mario Vargas Llosa (Nobel Prize, 2010); Andean music and textiles.

socialStructure.value: Mestizo majority; Indigenous and Afro-Peruvian communities.

sharedIdentity.value: Pride in the Inca heritage and Peruvian cuisine.

dailyLife.value: City apartments and self-built houses in Lima; adobe houses in the Andes; rice, potatoes, ceviche.

neighbours.value: Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Bolivia and Chile.

ideasReligions.value: Liberation theology began with the Peruvian priest Gustavo Gutiérrez.

colonisation.value: A former Spanish colony (Viceroyalty of Peru).

riseSignals.value: Independence declared by San Martín in 1821.

sources.value: Wikipedia: Peru; Wikipedia: History of Peru.
